b: 15-year-old IM Khuong Duy Dau won his first-ever 3 0 Thursday title in the first tournament on November 19, just six days after he won his first Freestyle Friday tournament. Later that day, GM Sina Movahed won his fifth title in the second tournament, and GM Vladimir Fedoseev won his second title in the final event.
First Tournament: Dau Wins First Eight Games, Cruises To Victory

Dau dominated the first tournament of the day. He started with eight consecutive wins, showing both attacking brilliance and accurate endgame technique. He scored a quick knockout against GM Sam Sevian in the sixth round.
In the next round, Dau kept the initiative throughout a long ending.

After victories in the first eight rounds, Dau drew IM Havard Haug in an accurate game. He won in the 10th round against GM Sergey Drygalov, before clinching first place with a draw against his countryman GM Nguyen Ngoc Truong Son. That brought Dau to 10 points, a full point ahead of GMs Zhamsaran Tsydypov, Rasmus Svane, Shant Sargsyan, and Truong Son, who tied for second through fifth place. WIM Melika Mohammadi took the top women's prize with seven points.
The top 10 finishers in the first tournament.
Second Tournament: Movahed Punishes Aggressive Openings To Take First

In the second event of the day Movahed used a winning streak in the fifth through 10th rounds to take first place. In the ninth round he scored a crushing win against GM Sergei Zhigalko's Evans Gambit.
In the next round Movahed broke apart GM Jeffery Xiong's stonewall setup.

In the final round, Haug needed to defeat Movahed with Black to pass him for first place. However, Movahed kept control, drawing by repetition in just 25 moves. That brought him to 9.5 points, half a point ahead of Haug and IM Renato Terry, who took second and third respectively. IM Karina Ambartsumova was the top scoring woman with six points, her 24th time taking the that prize!
The top 10 finishers in the second tournament.
Third Tournament: Fedoseev Turns The Tables To Take Title

In the third tournament, Fedoseev repeatedly overcame difficult positions in several games. In the fourth round he lost material early on against GM Tuan Minh Le, but found an endgame tactic to win a piece and the game.

Fedoseev managed an even bigger turnaround in the seventh round against GM Pablo Salinas Herrera. White played a beautiful game, and even had a forced mate in four moves before one mistake allowed Black's counterattack to decide the game.

Fedoseev's resourceful play brought him nine points. He was able to edge GM Shant Sargsyan on tiebreaks, while Xiong took third, half a point back. Oddly enough, both the second and third place finishers beat the winner in their head-to-head games. IM Nurgyul Salimova took advantage of a four-game winning streak to take the women's prize with seven points.

3 0 Thursday is a set of three weekly Swiss tournaments for verified titled players featuring their favorite time control. Each of the three tournaments is an 11-round Swiss with a 3+0 time control. The combined prize fund is $3,000 every week.
